conclusion.recommended_scope: Frame-mode only, additive per-recorded-stream report sections for current skill/observation branch and recharge-reference branch. Expose supplied intervals, target scope, animation-parameter qualification, event array counts and first/last relative frame/time references. Existing totals, event graphs, estimate flags, old sections, and all three formatters remain untouched.
conclusion.source_claim_limit: This is visibility of current existing reference data, not additional scheduling or verification of game mechanics.

current_source.finding: Only the aggregate initial/duration/cycle/recharge estimates appear in timing.

execution metrics choose next first streams element where unit equals current operator; only this skill/current-observation primary exposes interval/windup/recovery/first release/first impact/fixed delay.
Independent streams and recharge streams are traversed only to emit deduplicated original-animation-reference notes; their intervals and event arrays are absent from normal report metrics.
Each frame stream has explicit unit, scope, qualification, current-window frame arrays, emitted frame arrays, relative seconds, per-attack intervals and optional exact known fixed-delay source.
Stored frame values and event seconds subtract self.offset. Recharge-relative zero is its own phase origin; do not silently add duration or initial to manufacture a global time.
Reported timing uses shown/current-observation plan, with separate normal-plan recharge_streams. A short current branch is not the whole independent cast plan.
Alias paths similarly generate normal reference at offset=duration, then store relative normal streams as recharge_streams.

hazards.rule: Absent/None event arrays remain unknown or omitted; a supplied empty array can report zero supplied reference events but first/last time remain None. Do not use get(key,[]) for counts that would turn missing into confirmed zero.

Skill/current-observation and recharge times are separate phase-relative coordinates. Do not stitch streams into an absolute deployment/first-cast timeline. Initial and skill duration can be unknown. Only explicit source-relative references are displayed.

known_animation means available windup/reference parameters; reference_binding can mean a selected reference. Frame streams set exact_binding=False. None/absent flag is not False. Do not call any of these real client binding proof.

phase_clock_unbound, parameter_clock_only, or resource_and_damage_shared_clock=False must produce qualification and must not be overridden by numerical stream references. Preserve every unknown amount/phase estimate.

Deepcolor creates one representative token stream even for summon_count=0 and repeats component event times for summon_count>1 (operator_engine.py 348–352). The stream count is not actual deployment quantity or aggregate hits; do not multiply or describe it as all summons.

Shu S3 separate damage/healing (operator_engine.py 394–398), Mizuki separate regular and talent (608–614) can record same-unit streams. Preserve phase+index uniqueness and source order, no deduplication or aggregate sum.

A repeated timestamp can be distinct supplied events; retain multiplicity and order. Component multi-hit counts can exceed release count. Do not set() arrays or infer hit counts/damage from stream lengths.

damage.py 133–134 can intentionally replace times_seconds with emitted_times_seconds for alias full-cast attribution while impact_frames remains window-bounded. Never assert these arrays must share lengths; label/frame-array selection separately. Emitted array in a short shown branch describes its own emitted events, not all independent full-cast events.

interval_seconds/interval_frames are final produced scalar interval, not a constant for every event when temporary_attack_speed or per-attack intervals differ. Expose existing interval_frames_by_attack min/max only under explicit reference label if needed; no future extrapolation.

A stream may be acquisition/ordinary-action parameter reference even where component times were removed and actual_total=None (Gnosis S1, Mei S1, shield declaration). New visibility must not populate these component clocks. Preserve unplaced_components disclosure.

Ordinary continuous attacks often return a stream without adding it to self.streams; only deployment-speed continuous path appends (timing.py 249–267). Do not reconstruct from components or reported hits, and do not frame-round the continuous times. Recommended first scope excludes continuous.

An empty enemy range or zero enemy lifetime does not cancel independent friendly potential healing; keep target_scope and target_scope_notes. Range exit alone does not cancel a locked projectile; disappearance may remove emitted impacts without removing release references.

safe_metrics: supplied interval_seconds/interval_frames (qualify scalar on varying cadence)
supplied release_frames length/first/last, frame and derived seconds with actual timing fps
supplied impact_frames length/first/last (current branch bounded reference)
supplied emitted_impact_frames length/first/last (this branch emitted reference, may include tail)
optional existing fixed_impact_delay_seconds per supported owner stream only

required_notes: All event times are relative to this displayed reference phase; recharge starts at its own relative zero.
Stream records are scheduling/reference samples; counts do not equal deployed summon quantities, damage segments, or actual game hit counts.
Unplaced or phase-unbound outputs remain unknown and are not added to these streams.
Current displayed branch emitted events do not guarantee complete independent cast enumeration.
